h: Racing Tips and a Bit of Movie Magic
p: Want to knock a few tenths off? Keep your hands steady, your inputs smooth and your eyes up. New drivers tend to stamp on the brakes and saw at the wheel, which just scrubs off speed. The quickest laps usually come once you stop fighting the kart and let it flow through the bends.

Arrive in good time, wear trainers rather than anything with a heel, and if you've got long hair, bring a bobble to tie it back. Bring a water bottle too, because a full session under a helmet is thirstier work than you'd imagine.

When it comes to the rest of the day, Watford has a few aces up its sleeve. The big one for film fans is the Warner Bros. Studio Tour London, The Making of Harry Potter, out at Leavesden on the edge of town. Tickets must be booked ahead, so sort that well before you travel. Closer to the centre, Watford Museum tells the town's story, and the Watford Palace Theatre puts on everything from drama to the Christmas panto. The Grand Union Canal winds along the edge of Cassiobury Park, and neighbouring Whippendell Woods is great for a leafy walk once the adrenaline wears off.
